A.explanation: Distance $p$ is from single slit to double slit and does not appear in fringe spacing, so changing it affects brightness not spacing.

B.explanation: Distance $q$ is the double-slit separation $a$, and $x = \lambda D/a$ so smaller $a$ gives larger fringe spacing $x$.

C.explanation: Distance $r$ is the double-slit to screen distance $D$, and $x$ is proportional to $D$ so decreasing $r$ decreases spacing.

D.explanation: Fringe spacing $x$ is proportional to wavelength $\lambda$, so decreasing $\lambda$ decreases spacing.

hints: Look at the diagram labels: $q$ is the separation of the two slits in the double slit and $r$ is the distance from the double slit to the screen.
Recall the double-slit fringe spacing relation $x = \lambda D / a$, where $a$ is slit separation and $D$ is slit-to-screen distance.
Check which change makes the numerator larger or the denominator smaller, since $x$ increases when $\lambda$ or $D$ increases or $a$ decreases.
walkthrough: Identify the symbols from the diagram: $q$ is the slit separation $a$, $r$ is the slit-to-screen distance $D$, and $p$ only sets how light reaches the double slit.
State the governing rule for double-slit interference: fringe spacing $x = \lambda D / a$, where $\lambda$ is the wavelength of light.
Use proportionality: $x$ increases if $\lambda$ increases, if $D$ increases, or if $a$ decreases.
Test each change: decreasing $p$ does not change $x$, decreasing $r$ decreases $D$ so decreases $x$, and decreasing $\lambda$ decreases $x$.
Decreasing $q$ decreases $a$ in the denominator, so $x = \lambda r / q$ becomes larger. This is option B.
